questions.question: By default, what kind of component is a file inside the app/ directory?
questions.explanation: Components in app/ are Server Components unless the file starts with "use client". Their JavaScript is never sent to the browser.

questions.question: What does hydration mean?
options: Compressing images before they are sent
Re-running database queries in the browser
React attaching event handlers to server-rendered HTML so it becomes interactive
questions.explanation: The server sends HTML first for a fast paint; the browser then loads Client Component JavaScript and React hydrates the existing markup.

questions.question: Which of these needs the "use client" directive?
options: A component that uses useState and an onClick handler
A component that awaits fetch() and renders a list
A layout that renders a header and children
A component that reads a database with a secret key
questions.explanation: State, effects and event handlers only work in the browser, so they require a Client Component. Data fetching and secrets belong on the server.

questions.question: In the URL /courses/react, what are `courses` and `react`?
options: Two route segments, each mapping to a folder in app/
questions.explanation: Each part of the path is a segment, and each segment corresponds to a folder under app/, whose special files (page, layout, loading, error) define its behaviour.
